On the Windows verification box (see memory note windows-build-machine), `shell_integration_harness` in its default mode (no arguments) fails on `jusprin-newui` at d89836f883, before any change. Reproduced 2026-09-24 in a build tree at C:\b\pcm configured from a worktree of that commit (-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF, Mesa provisioned with src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1).

Symptom: after `HARNESS CHECK spool_menu_lists_a_spool PASS` (check ~140) the app's log shows `Uncaught exception: missing enabled header menu item: Filament settings…`. That exception is thrown by `choose_header_item` in tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp (line ~2373), called from the spool-menu step right after `row->invoke_row_action()` via `m_frame->CallAfter` (line ~2599). GUI_RUN then returns 0 with no HARNESS RESULT, exit code 1. Two baseline runs failed the same way.

It is timing-sensitive: a build that added ~430 ms of GUI-thread work at the first Home snapshot got past this step every time, then failed `print_opens_cancellable_native_preflight` (verify_print_preflight, line ~2954). That check waits for the modal "Send print job" dialog, and the log showed SelectMachineDialog being constructed. The last recorded pass of that check on this machine was C:\b\full-default.err, 2026-09-21.

Task: find why the "Filament settings…" header item is missing or disabled right after picking a spool row: a race between the spool swap's queued events and the CallAfter, or a real regression in the header menu. Make the harness wait on the condition it needs instead of the event order. Then see whether the Print preflight check still fails once the run gets past this step. Run the default mode twice to confirm.

name: windows-build-machine
description: "Facts about the Windows Server 2022 machine used for JusPrin Windows verification (no admin, RDP at 100%, no GPU, toolchain and Mesa locations)"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory

The JusPrin Windows verification box (Windows Server 2022, user `guitest`, as of 2026-09-09): no admin rights, no GPU, reached over RDP at 100% scaling. VS 2022 Build Tools, CMake and Ninja are installed; the deps live at `C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`. Main checkout `C:/src/JusPrin` is on `jusprin-newui` with a Release build in `C:/src/JusPrin/build`.

**Why:** Several handoff items were blocked on machine facts (no debugger, no admin, DPI cannot change from inside an RDP session), so knowing them up front saves a diagnostic pass.

**How to apply:**
- GL needs Mesa, and **every freshly configured CMake build tree starts without it** — nothing in CMake or the repo supplies it. Run `pwsh src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1 -BuildDir <build dir> -Source C:\src\JusPrin\build\src\Release` after configuring; it copies `libgallium_wgl.dll` and `dxil.dll` (from `C:\Program Files (x86)\Windows Kits\10\Redist\D3D\x64\`) beside every GUI exe and `opengl32.dll` into its `mesa\` subfolder. Placement is not interchangeable, and each missing file has a silent signature — both documented in "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` (on `jusprin-newui` since 2026-09-13, commit `318208608f`).
- Quick recall of the signatures: no `libgallium_wgl.dll` → `glcontext not ready, postpone init`, no `got opengl version`, black canvas all session. No `dxil.dll` → d3d12 initializes, then exit `0x80070057` on the first canvas draw with nothing logged. Both verified by removing the file and re-running. With all three present, both `d3d12` (default, `4.2 … D3D12`) and `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` (`4.6 … llvmpipe`) render.
- `slow_bootup` only moves the dxil crash from startup to first canvas paint; it is not a workaround.
- Lesson: a clear-only WGL smoke test passed under d3d12 because clearing compiles no shader, and was wrongly read as clearing the driver. A smoke test that skips the suspect code path proves nothing about it. (That test was removed from the repo for this reason.)
- A first-run datadir (e.g. copies of `C:\b\dd3`) logs ~630k lines in the first minute — the `GuideFrame::GetFilamentInfo` profile scan, driver-independent. Not a GL symptom.
- `D3D12 (Microsoft Basic Render Driver)` in the log is **Mesa's own d3d12 gallium driver on WARP**, not Microsoft's GLon12 mapping layer and not a real GPU. Confirm which GL is live by listing the process's loaded modules: the bundled Mesa shows `<exe dir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` (+ `DXIL.dll` once d3d12 has drawn), the unprovisioned fallback shows only `C:\Windows\SYSTEM32\OPENGL32.dll`.
- The permission guard refuses `Remove-Item` under `C:\b` (it reports it as a protected path) and misparses `rd /s /q` and path-like string literals as delete targets. Hand build-tree deletion to the user; build trees there contain `resources` symlinks into live worktrees, so unlink those before any recursive delete.
- A debugger can be had without admin: download `https://aka.ms/windbg/download` (an .appinstaller pointing at a ~1.2 GB msixbundle), unzip the bundle, unzip `windbg_win-x64.msix`, and `amd64/cdb.exe` runs directly. Set `_NO_DEBUG_HEAP=1` when running the harness under cdb, or teardown crawls in the debug heap for many minutes.
- Fixture directories for the harness's visual modes must be short paths (e.g. `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\...`); a long scratchpad path makes the profile-bundle copy exceed MAX_PATH and the fixture slice never validates.
- The harness prints everything on stderr; the exit code must be read with `$LASTEXITCODE` in PowerShell (bash shows 127).
- DPI at 150%/200% needs the user to reconnect the RDP session at that scale. See [[jusprin-windows-parity-handoff]].

Node is installed twice: the older `C:\tools\node` (v24.20.0), which is **not on PATH**, and
`C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64` (v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0), added to the **user
PATH** on 2026-09-16. Check `Get-Command npm.cmd` before installing anything; a fresh Bash
session may still need `export PATH="$PATH:/c/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64"`.

npm is not optional any more: since commit `5fc0efe2e3` the Agent and Home pages are built from
TypeScript and their `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` is generated, not committed.
Without npm, CMake **fails at configure time** (`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt`
`FATAL_ERROR`), so the first new source file you add breaks the build tree; and without the
bundles the app creates no Agent WebView at all, which shows up as `shell_agent_webview_created
FAIL` / "the Agent page did not complete its handshake" in the shell harness. Build them with
`npm ci && npm run build` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` and `HomeUI`.

The shell harness and the Agent page must come from the same commit: a harness exe built before
a page change hangs at `agent_reply_streams_to_completion` instead of failing.

To work on `jusprin-mcp` (the MCP stdio helper) you do **not** need an app build, and a worktree
can have its own build tree in about three minutes: configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF`
(skips the npm requirement above) plus
`-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local`, then
`cmake --build <dir> --config Release --target jusprin-mcp -- -m`, which compiles only the six
bridge/registry sources and `main.cpp`. `vswhere.exe` is **not** installed; vcvars is at
`C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvars64.bat`
and cmake at `C:\tools\cmake\bin\cmake.exe`. Point the Python suite at the result with
`JUSPRIN_TEST_BRIDGE=<dir>\src\Release\jusprin-mcp.exe`; the whole suite runs in ~8 s.

An **existing** build tree configured before node was installed keeps `JUSPRIN_NPM:FILEPATH=JUSPRIN_NPM-NOTFOUND`
in its CMakeCache, and `find_program` never retries a cached NOTFOUND -- so the next build fails at
configure with the `npm not found` FATAL_ERROR even once npm is on PATH. Reconfigure the tree once with
`cmake . -DJUSPRIN_NPM="C:/Users/guitest/.local/node-v24.21.0-win-x64/npm.cmd"`; putting node on PATH alone
is not enough. Neither the Bash tool nor a PowerShell session started before 2026-09-16 inherits the user
PATH entry, so prefix `$env:PATH` explicitly in each invocation.

**Shared build tree (2026-09-17):** other Claude sessions build and commit from `C:\src\JusPrin` and
`C:\src\JusPrin\build` concurrently. Do not patch that checkout or build there from a worktree session;
a link there holds `.lib` files and breaks their build (LNK1104). Use a separate tree instead: configure
with `-DBUILD_TESTS=ON -DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF -DSLIC3R_MSVC_PDB=OFF -DDEP_BUILD_DIR=C:/src/JusPrin/deps/build`
at a short path such as `C:\b\wsh`, which is a full `libslic3r_gui` build of about 40 minutes. To symbolize a crash
without a debugger, relink with a `ForceImportAfterCppTargets` props file (Link `GenerateDebugInformation`/`GenerateMapFile`),
read the fault offset from the event log (Application, event 1000), and run
`llvm-symbolizer --obj=<exe> --relative-address <offset>` (the symbolizer ships in the MSVC bin dir).

- The in-app browser pane renders a `file://` page as a static snapshot and refuses `screenshot`.
  To look at a rendered page (e.g. a vitest `PREVIEW_OUT` page), serve the directory over a
  throwaway node http server on 127.0.0.1 and navigate to that instead.

**Commits can hang in the `entire` hook (2026-09-25):** `git commit` from an agent session in a worktree
never returned; `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` alone hangs too (60 s, no output,
stdin closed). `--no-verify` does not skip prepare-commit-msg, and hooks must not be bypassed anyway, so
stop after one timed attempt (`timeout 90 git commit ... < /dev/null`), kill the orphaned `entire`
process it leaves behind (`ps -W | grep entire`), and ask Kenneth. Other sessions' commits carry an
`Entire-Checkpoint` trailer, so the hook works somewhere; the cause was not found.

name: windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop
description: How to drive real JusPrin UI gestures on the Windows box when the RDP session is disconnected (SetCursorPos and screen capture both die; send WM_ messages and read geometry instead)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: c818cfcf-07b0-4d84-a4d6-a69c1bd9fdde
  modified: 2026-09-09T22:06:52.556Z
---

When the RDP session to the Windows verification box is **disconnected** (`query session` shows state `Disc` for the `guitest` session), `SetCursorPos`/`mouse_event` silently do nothing — `GetCursorPos` keeps returning 0,0 — and `Graphics.CopyFromScreen` throws "The handle is invalid". Only a *connected* session has an input desktop.

**Why:** This looks exactly like an application bug — gestures appear to have no effect and screenshots fail — so it can burn a long time before you realise the session, not the code, is the problem.

**How to apply:**
- Check `query session` first when input or capture stops working.
- Real UI testing still works without a desktop: `SendMessageTimeout` WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_MOUSEMOVE / WM_LBUTTONUP / WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK straight to the child HWND. This goes through the real wxMSW window procedure, real `SetCapture`, and real double-click handling — strictly more real than the harness's `ProcessEvent` injection, which bypasses `MSWWindowProc` entirely.
- A faithful drag must hold the pointer at a fixed **screen** x and recompute the client x from the target window's live `GetWindowRect` each step. Holding client x fixed makes a moving splitter run away, because the app converts with `ClientToScreen` against the window's current position.
- Read results from `EnumChildWindows` + `GetWindowRect` rather than pixels; assert that sibling columns tile the client rect exactly, which catches overlaps a per-window size check cannot see.
- P/Invoke `GetWindowTextW` must be declared `CharSet=CharSet.Unicode`, or the StringBuilder is marshalled as ANSI and the W call overruns the buffer and crashes PowerShell.
- The harness holds `shell_integration_harness.exe` open; kill it before relinking or the link fails with LNK1104.
- See [[windows-build-machine]] for the Mesa/GL and toolchain facts.

On the Home screen (2026-09-12) I shipped a review-ready branch after passing every
guard, then the user immediately found two things I never tried: the Agent chat panel
was still on screen, and clicking a project card led nowhere useful. Both were one
click away.

**Why:** I checked the *page* against the mockup instead of the *screen*, and I stopped
at "synthetic input is blocked on this machine" instead of finding another way in.
Worse, my capture method was `PrintWindow`, which renders OpenGL content black **and
omits modal dialogs entirely** — so my "verification" screenshots were structurally
blind to exactly the defects that were there. I verified with an instrument I never
validated.

**How to apply:**
- Before trusting a screenshot, prove the capture shows what is really on screen.
  `PrintWindow` lies about GL and modals; `CopyFromScreen` of the window rect does not.
- Drive the page's own controls over the WebView2 DevTools protocol when the OS refuses
  synthetic input: launch with `REDACTED`,
  then `Runtime.evaluate` a real `element.click()` on the target. See
  [[windows-ui-testing-without-a-desktop]]. That click goes through the real handler and
  the real bridge, and it found two more defects the guards could not.
- Run the screen's primary gesture end to end in the app before calling UI work done,
  and compare the whole window against the design, not just the surface you wrote.
- Config levers that remove blockers without clicking: `default_page=1` lands on the
  editor, `no_warn_when_modified_gcodes=true` suppresses the customized-preset modal,
  `backup_switch=false` stops the restore prompt.

On the Windows box (2026-09-24, Entire CLI 0.11.0), `git commit` in any JusPrin worktree can sit forever in
`.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg`, which runs `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg ... || true`. Nothing is
logged to `.entire/logs/entire.log` while it waits; it seems to wait on keyboard input the agent's shell cannot give.
Two sessions hit it the same evening (the Undo commit and the setup-flow Done commit), and both sat 10-40 minutes.

**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.

**How to apply:** Run commits in the background. If the commit has not landed after a couple of minutes, find
the `entire` process started by that commit (`ps -W | grep /entire`, check its start time) and kill only that
PID. The hook's `|| true` lets git finish, and later hooks (commit-msg, post-commit, post-rewrite) have gone through
normally. Do not pass `--no-verify`. A second commit right after (the rebase) did not hang, so it is intermittent.
See [[windows-build-machine]].

The Windows parity handoff for `jusprin-newui` is `C:\Users\guitest\Downloads\jusprin-windows-captures\windows-parity-handoff.md` (stale: written before the fixes), with `windows-parity-results-2026-09-09.md` beside it describing what was fixed. New captures from 2026-09-09 are under `C:\Users\guitest\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\wp\caps`.

**Why:** The fixes were merged into jusprin-newui and pushed on 2026-09-10 (fa046ccc exit crash, 1bdb4fbd post_init gate, 4cca01e3 dark-ui/handshake/recomputing-capture, 8162b651 font size; combined default run 346 checks, exit 0). The branches `claude/windows-parity-handoff-ed77fe` and `claude/windows-font-size-fix` are now merged history. The handoff doc and the screenshot review predate them; findings 1-3 of the review (split button, disabled re-slice with no reason, blank Preview under llvmpipe) are still open.

**How to apply:**
- Worktrees: `C:/src/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/windows-parity-handoff-ed77fe` (has a Release build) and `C:/src/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/windows-font-size-fix` (has a Release build of the harness target only). Both harness builds carry Mesa DLLs next to the exe.
- Item 1 (exit 0xC0000409): uncaught `boost::filesystem::remove_all` exception escaping `main` (the log sink keeps `log/debug_*.log.0` open), plus a latent 0xC0000005: the shell controller's static slot destroyed after the Plater. Verified exit 0 in every mode in that worktree.
- Item 2 (Home tab): upstream `GUI_App::post_init` runs from the first idle event and ends with `select_tab(0)`. Platform-independent.
- Item 3 (dark mode): on Windows only `dark_color_mode` in the app config matters.
- Item 4 (DPI): 200% captured in `Downloads\jusprin-windows-captures\2026-09-09-pass2-200dpi`. 150% still open (needs `LogPixels=144` + `Win8DpiScaling=1` in `HKCU:\Control Panel\Desktop` and a sign-out). Capture popups by screen blit with a DPI-aware process, never PrintWindow.
- Font size on Windows (screenshot-review finding 4, measured 2026-09-09): `Label::sysFont` truncates `size*4/5` to int points, wx MSW then rounds `pt*96/72`, so the 14 px body role renders at 15 px, 10 at 11, 18 at 19, 24 at 25; only 12 is exact. Not hinting (GDI vs unhinted widths within 1%). Fix belongs in fork-owned `ShellTheme::font`: `SetFractionalPointSize(size * 72.0 / 96.0)` on non-Apple, and `mono_font` should use `GetFractionalPointSize`.
See [[windows-build-machine]].

My own clean build of d89836f883 is still compiling at `C:\b\vh`, so nothing is confirmed yet. I'll pick this up when it finishes.

**Leading theory for the spool-menu failure:** a race in the harness, not a broken menu.
- Picking a spool row asks the popup menu to rebuild itself into the row's submenu (`HeaderMenu::CallAfter` in `HeaderControls.cpp:555-561`).
- The harness then queues its own `m_frame->CallAfter` to press "Filament settings…".
- wx runs queued events one object at a time, finishing everything queued on one before starting the next. If the main window already had something waiting, the harness's step runs first, while the spool list is still showing. "Filament settings…" isn't on the spool list, so the step throws.
- That fits the timing sensitivity: adding ~430 ms of work at the first Home snapshot would drain the main window's queue beforehand.

The planned fix is to wait until the visible menu has an enabled "Filament settings…" row, using the harness's existing `wait_until`, instead of relying on event order.

**Print preflight:** a failing run's app log (`jusprin-shell-78f0-f3b5-7299`) shows the "Send print job" dialog (`SelectMachineDialog`) was constructed, but the harness had moved on to slice-all within about 40 ms. So `ShowModal()` either never started its loop or was closed almost at once. Print all, which reuses the same dialog, passes. None of the commits since 09-21 show an obvious cause yet.

To tell these apart, the first run uses temporary logging; none of it will be in the final change:
- **Harness (`shell_harness.cpp`):** which menu rows are showing when the step runs, and whether events were already queued.
- **Menu:** when the row's submenu rebuild actually runs.
- **Print path:** the `ShowModal` return code, how long the step took, and how many 50 ms timer ticks saw the dialog.

I've also built the Agent and Home web pages from this commit and moved my worktree branch to d89836f883.

Next: run the default mode, read the logs, apply the wait, remove the logging, then run it twice and report on both checks.

Both failures were timing problems in the harness, not bugs in the app. After the fix, two default-mode runs both passed: exit 0, 416 checks each (the old 414 plus two new wait checks). I built my own tree at `C:\b\vh` from a clean d89836f883, with the Agent and Home pages built from that commit. The only change is in [shell_harness.cpp](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp), and nothing is committed.

**"Filament settings…" missing: a race.** Clicking a spool row's ⋯ button doesn't rebuild the menu right away. The popup queues the rebuild with its own `CallAfter` (`HeaderControls.cpp:555-561`). The harness then queued its next step with `m_frame->CallAfter`. wx empties one object's queue completely before moving to the next, in the order the objects first queued something. So if the main window already had any event queued, the harness step ran before the menu rebuilt. It found the spool list still showing and threw.
- **Reproduced:** my ~25 normal runs never hit it. When I queued one empty event on the main window first, I got your exact symptom every time: the spool list rows, then `Uncaught exception: missing enabled header menu item: Filament settings…`, then `GUI_RUN RETURNED 0`.
- **The menu itself is fine:** in every run where the rebuild went first, "Filament settings…" was there and enabled.
- **Fix:** the step now waits until the visible menu has an enabled "Filament settings…" row (new check `spool_row_menu_opens`). With the forced bad ordering, the run now passes.

**Print preflight: fails for a different reason.** The dialog wasn't the problem. In the failing run, `request_action(Print)` returned after 0 ms without opening anything, because no plate had a valid slice (`sliced_count=0`, header offering Slice). The `SelectMachineDialog` in your log came from the Print all step, which runs after slice-all.
- **Why the slice goes stale:** the header-setup steps change the printer and filament presets after the plate was sliced. Orca doesn't apply a settings change to the print right away; it waits 500 ms on a one-shot timer (`Plater.cpp:7743`).
- **Pass or fail depends on that timer:** if it hasn't fired when Print is checked, the old slice still counts as valid and the dialog opens (pass). If it has fired, the slice is correctly invalid and Print isn't offered (fail). The extra 430 ms in your timing build moved that timer ahead of the check. I saw this fail once in about 25 runs.
- **Fix:** before the Print check, the harness applies the pending change immediately with `Plater::update(false, true)`, the call the header's own Slice button makes. It re-slices if that invalidated the plate, then waits until the header offers an enabled Print (new check `print_offered_for_current_settings`).

**Things you should know:**
- **WebView2 clash between sessions:** another session's harness, `C:\b\pcm\...\shell_integration_harness.exe --home-printers-live`, is still running and holds the shared WebView2 profile folder `%LOCALAPPDATA%\JusPrin2\EBWebView`. Any harness started alongside it fails immediately at `shell_agent_page_handshake_complete`, which says nothing about the code. I left that process alone and ran mine with `WEBVIEW2_USER_DATA_FOLDER=C:\b\vh-webview`. I've added this to the memory notes.
- **Result line lost:** when `choose_header_item` throws inside a queued call, the harness never prints a `HARNESS RESULT` line; the run just exits 1. I didn't change that. Having it report the failure instead of throwing would make the next race easier to spot.
- **Same 500 ms gap in the app:** real users see it too. For up to 500 ms after a preset change, the header still offers Print on a slice that's out of date. Stock Orca's own Print button behaves the same way, so I left it alone.

The Print check needs a current slice, and whether it had one depended on timing. The steps before it change the printer and filament settings. If the Print check ran before that delay was up, the old slice still counted and the test passed; if it ran after, the slice was out of date, Print wasn't offered, and the test failed.

**The fix:** before the Print check, the harness applies the pending settings change right away, using the same call the Slice button uses. It then slices again and waits until Print is actually offered. The change is one new step in [shell_harness.cpp](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp), adding one check, `print_offered_for_current_settings`.

**Proof it no longer depends on timing:** I ran once with a temporary log line after the settings are applied. It showed the slice was out of date at that point, so the fix re-sliced before checking Print.
